lane: فِنْدِيرٌ (S, K) and فِنْدِيرَةٌ (S, M, K) A great mass of rock that projects, or juts out, (تَنْدُرُ,) from the head of a mountain: (S:) what is thus called is short of (دُونَ) what is termed فِدْرَة [in relation to a mountain]; (M, K;) by which may be meat دون in respect of place and projection, not in respect of size. (TA.) [See also فِدْرَةٌ and فَادِرَةٌ: and see more in art. فندر.] فِنْدِيرٌ and ↓فِنْدِيرَةٌ (K in this art., and S in art. فدر,) A great mass of rock that becomes detached (S, K) from the head (S) or from the side (K) of a mountain: (S, K:) pl. فَنَادِيرُ. (TA.) === And, both words, A large lump of dates (K, TA) compacted together; as also فِدْرَةٌ. (TA.)

entries.text: الفندير، بالكسر وبالهاء: قطعة ضخمة من تمر، والصخرة العظيمة تنقلع عن عرض الجبل.
